prompt.title: High-throughput Kafka with transactional outbox and idempotent consumer

variables.var: aggregate whose state changes publish events
topic, following the team's naming rule
group id of the consuming service
polling relay, or Debezium outbox event router (CDC)

var.name: event_catalog
var.example: OrderPlaced{orderId, lines[], amount, currency}; OrderCancelled{orderId, reason}

variables.var: events, fields and versions from SPEC.md

var.name: throughput
var.example: peak 3,000 events/s, p99 end-to-end under 2 s, 12 partitions

context.platform: Spring Boot 4.1.2 managed versions: Spring Kafka 4.1.2, kafka-clients 4.2.2, PostgreSQL JDBC 42.7.14, Testcontainers 2.0.5. Producer idempotence and acks=all are kafka-clients defaults since 3.0; state them explicitly anyway.

instructions.step: Name the failure in the current code: which crash points lose an event, which publish an event for a rolled-back change, and which reorder events.

Design the outbox table and its partial index for unpublished rows, and the writer that inserts one outbox row per event inside the same transaction as the {{aggregate}} change. Generate the event id at write time.

Implement the {{relay}} relay. For polling: claim a batch with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED ordered by id, publish with key = aggregate id, wait for the broker acknowledgement, then mark the rows published in the same transaction; size the batch and poll interval from the load targets.

Implement the consumer in {{consumer_group}}: in one local transaction, insert (consumer_group, event_id) into processed_events and apply the effect; a duplicate key means skip. Acknowledge the offset only after that transaction commits.
Add error handling: DefaultErrorHandler with bounded exponential back-off, non-retryable exception classification, and DeadLetterPublishingRecoverer to {{topic}}.DLT with the original headers.
If the use case spans services, write the saga as explicit steps with a compensation for each, driven by events, each step idempotent by event id.
Write the Testcontainers tests listed in the verification section, run them, and report.

invariants.inv: No broker send inside a database transaction that also changes state; the only path to Kafka is the outbox.
The event id is created when the outbox row is written and never changes across relay retries.
The consumer's effect and its processed_events insert commit in one local transaction; the offset is acknowledged after it.
The record key is the aggregate id, so all events of one aggregate share a partition and keep their order.
Two relay instances running together publish each row at most once per claim (SKIP LOCKED), and a crashed relay's rows are re-claimed.
processed_events retention is longer than the longest possible redelivery window (relay outage plus consumer lag plus DLT replay), stated in hours.
The traceparent from the originating request travels in the outbox headers to the Kafka record headers.

anti_goals.no: No exactly-once claims: the delivery is at-least-once and the effect is idempotent; say so in the design.
No Kafka transactions as a substitute for the outbox; they do not cover the database write.
No unbounded retries and no retrying of deserialization or validation errors.
No payload schema change without a new event version.

output_contract.file: outbox and processed_events migration with indexes
ADR: outbox and at-least-once delivery, with the retention arithmetic
output_contract.report: For each invariant, the test that proves it and its result; the measured relay throughput from the test.

verification.check: OutboxIT: roll back the use case transaction; assert no outbox row and no Kafka record.
OutboxIT: kill the relay after publish and before mark (test hook); after restart, the duplicate record carries the same event id.
IdempotentConsumerIT: deliver each event twice and after a consumer crash before ack; the effect is applied once.
OrderingIT: 1,000 events for 10 aggregates arrive in per-aggregate order.
RelayConcurrencyIT: two relays on one table; every row published, none twice within one claim cycle.
The ADR states the window components and the retention, and the cleanup job uses that value.
OutboxIT: the consumed record's traceparent header equals the request's.

prompt.task: Replace the dual write in the current code with the transactional outbox, relay and idempotent consumer for {{aggregate}} events on {{topic}}, proving every invariant with the tests above.
